corpusSummary: Across 2026 papers, the corpus maps how large language models intersect society, learning, policy, and research practice. It highlights LLMs as tools for analysis, design, and decision support, while exposing persistent concerns about bias, safety, accountability, and anthropomorphism. The records show shifting emphasis toward user trust, ethical governance, educational integration, and culturally grounded assessments, with a strong call for validation and responsible deployment.

themes.name: LLMs as research tools and methodological shifts
themes.description: The corpus documents growing use of LLMs for data extraction, coding, simulation, and analytical workflows across disciplines, with emphasis on validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and adoption
themes.description: A broad set of studies investigates user interaction with AI across health, education, parenting, design, and crisis contexts, focusing on trust, privacy, social influence, and barriers and enablers to adoption.

themes.name: Education, learning, and AI literacy
themes.description: Work spans AI-assisted learning, tutoring, scaffolding, and literacy development, alongside concerns about dependency, ethics, and the evolving role of teachers and curricula.

themes.name: Safety, bias, and ethics in LLMs
themes.description: Multiple studies assess fairness, safety, misinformation, fallibility, and cultural adequacy, advocating standardized protocols and responsible deployment.
